CA1972A.wouldSay: Heart of Gold, Sweet City Woman, Lightfoot, the Guess Who - that's CHAB the year I got my licence. Then it turns into my grandfather's 78s, Lombardo and some French soldier song, and I'd reach for the dial.
missing: Ocean - Put Your Hand in the Hand (1971)

Stompin' Tom Connors - Bud the Spud (1969)
CA1972A.fake: After five right songs, eleven of sixteen seeds are 1930s-40s records (three Lombardo, Piaf, Tino Rossi, two Christmas songs) that no Prairie teenager in 1972 played or heard as his own.
CA1972A.missingScene: The CanCon-era rock wave (Lighthouse, April Wine, Crowbar, Five Man Electrical Band, Chilliwack), TV country and old-time (Tommy Hunter, Stompin' Tom, Don Messer fiddle), and 1960s Canadian pop (Ian & Sylvia, Bobby Curtola, early Guess Who) - the list jumps from 1949 straight to 1970. Unsure whether 'Marriage Vow' got any Prairie airplay after its 1949 run; I only knew 'I'm Movin' On'.

CA1976A.wouldSay: Charlebois, Harmonium, puis le phoque en Alaska... ça, c'est mon frère avec sa guitare sur la galerie, l'été des Olympiques. Après ça, ça vire en radio anglaise de Toronto.
missing: Beau Dommage - Le blues d'la métropole (1975)
Ginette Reno - Un peu plus haut, un peu plus loin (1975 Saint-Jean)
CA1976A.fake: Only three French songs out of sixteen, then a block of 1970-72 English-Canadian AM hits and a 1949 Hank Snow side; Hotel California was a 1977 hit, not 1976.
CA1976A.missingScene: Quebec disco and variety (Boule Noire, Toulouse, Patsy Gallant, René Simard, Michel Louvain), the chansonniers and Saint-Jean anthems (Vigneault, Ferland, Dubois, Dufresne, Les Séguin), country-western québécois (Willie Lamothe, Paul Brunelle), and the hits from France that ruled Quebec radio (Dassin, Fugain). 'Pour un instant' and 'La complainte du phoque' are 1974 but were still everywhere in 1976.

CA1976B.missingScene: The whole Quebec scene at its peak: Harmonium, Beau Dommage, Charlebois, Vigneault, Dufresne, Ferland, Octobre, Offenbach; Quebec disco (Boule Noire, Toulouse, Patsy Gallant); France's hits; country-western québécois. CA1984B.fake: A four-song 1940s block (Hank Snow and three Guy Lombardo) plus Piaf sits in the middle of a 1984 list, and Summer of '69 was a 1985 single although the album came out in November 1984.
CA1984B.missingScene: Nothing between 1950 and 1980: no 1970s Canadian classics that were still on the radio (Guess Who, BTO, Lightfoot, April Wine, Trooper), and no Toronto new wave beyond Parachute Club (Spoons, Platinum Blonde, Rough Trade, Martha and the Muffins).
